subject: Urban Planning
title: Love Canal: Poison Beneath the Playground
description: A fast breakdown of Love Canal: Poison Beneath the Playground for builders.

hook.text: In the 1970s, children in Love Canal, New York played on a field built over 21,000 tons of buried toxic waste.

buildup.text: Hooker Chemical dumped waste there from 1942 to 1953, then sold the land to the school board for $1.

discovery.text: Chemicals seeped into basements. Birth defects and cancer rates soared. Black sludge oozed through lawns.

twist.text: The deed included a warning about buried chemicals. The school board built on it anyway. No one read the fine print.

climax.text: President Carter declared a federal emergency. 800 families were relocated. The EPA Superfund program was born.

punchline.text: They built a school on poison. The law to prevent it came 30 years late.

quiz.question: What federal program was created in response to Love Canal?
options: The Clean Air Act enforcement division
The EPA Superfund program for toxic waste cleanup
